cold_email.subject: Interest in Educator / West Acres Mall — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educator / West Acres Mall opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Training Coordinator opportunity with Schneider Electric at Schneider Electric.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. cold_email.body:
Dear Northwestern Mutual Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Financial Planning - Educators Welcome opportunity with Northwestern Mutual at Northwestern Mutual.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Professional Service leadership development program — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear FutureTech Insights Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Professional Service leadership development program opportunity with FutureTech Insights at FutureTech Insights.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Lab Coordinator - Health Tech Innovation — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Coforge Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Lab Coordinator - Health Tech Innovation opportunity with Coforge at Coforge.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Dear Associated Students, Inc. at California State University Long Beach Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Marketing Assistant opportunity with Associated Students, Inc. at California State University Long Beach at Associated Students, Inc. at California State University Long Beach.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Sr Structured Finance Execution Lead
jobs.description: About the Team The Capital Markets team develops the financing strategy, solutions, and partnerships needed to support our expanding global AI infrastructure platform and long-term investment plans. About the Role We’re looking for a senior structured finance leader to create immediate execution leverage for a growing capital markets function. In this role, you’ll take broad financing objectives, such as raising a large pool of capital from a defined set of counterparties, and independently turn them into well-run transaction processes. You’ll lead complex financings from strategy through close, manage counterparties and advisors, and bring sound judgment to capital structure, risk allocation, process design, and execution. This is a hands-on role for someone who is still close to the details, not a purely senior relationship manager. Your work will allow the team lead to spend less time in day-to-day execution and more time building the broader capital markets organization. In this role, you will: - Lead large, complex financing processes from initial structuring through diligence, negotiation, documentation, and closing. - Translate broad capital-raising objectives into executable financing plans, timelines, work streams, and counterparty strategies. - Manage lenders, investors, advisors, counsel, and internal stakeholders across high-stakes transactions. - Provide oversight on financial structuring, modeling, diligence, risk allocation, and transaction documentation. - Make clear recommendations on financing strategy, counterparty selection, process design, and tradeoffs. - Operate effectively in a small, high-impact team without relying on a large analyst or associate bench. - Help build repeatable internal processes for a financing function that is still scaling. - Coach and develop more junior transaction professionals. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 10-15 years of experience executing structured finance, project finance, infrastructure finance, digital infrastructure finance, or other capital-intensive transactions. - Personally led multiple complex or large-scale financings through close, with the ability to explain your individual role and decisions in detail. - Experience across the full transaction lifecycle, including structuring, modeling oversight, lender or investor engagement, documentation, diligence, negotiation, and closing. - Strong judgment across capital structure, counterparties, risk allocation, and financing process design. - Bank training, ideally followed by a successful move into an in-house, principal, developer, infrastructure investment, or specialist advisory environment. - Exposure to data centers, digital infrastructure, power, energy, infrastructure, or similarly capital-intensive sectors. - Experience building financing processes or functions, rather than only operating within a mature platform. - A track record of managing, coaching, or developing junior transaction professionals. - Comfort operating in a low-hierarchy, high-ambiguity environment where senior leaders are expected to stay close to execution. - Willingness to relocate to or work consistently from San Francisco. cold_email.subject: Interest in Internal Communications Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear The University of Huddersfield Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Internal Communications Coordinator opportunity with The University of Huddersfield at The University of Huddersfield.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Technical Business Development Representative
jobs.location: Hybrid - San Francisco, New York City, Austin
jobs.description: About Vercel: Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience. Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide. About the Role: As a Technical Business Development Representative, you'll be the first point of contact for companies that submit inbound leads, and you'll qualify them with personalized outreach to engineering and product leaders. You'll work closely with Account Executives to turn those conversations into pipeline in the commercial segment. In your first 6 to 12 months, you'll learn the SaaS sales cycle directly from sales and product leaders and build the foundation for a career in go-to-market. This is a hybrid role with 3 in-office days per week in San Francisco, New York City, or Austin. jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, SPACE - Sandbox Platform)
jobs.description: ABOUT THE ROLE SPACE is Perplexity's sandbox platform. It's the isolated execution layer behind Perplexity Computer, the public Sandbox API, and a growing set of agent products. Every time an agent writes code, runs a tool, opens a browser, builds an app, or works on a user's files, it runs inside a SPACE sandbox. We built our own sandbox platform that lets us build the exact platform our products need: real pause and resume, forking, rolling snapshots, credential isolation, fine-grained network policy, and enterprise-grade encryption. The work spans low-level virtualization and networking, distributed state machines, petabyte storage, and careful API design. Reliability, security, and cold-start latency are all things our customers feel directly. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Design and build core sandbox infrastructure for running untrusted, agent-generated code safely, quickly, and at scale. - Own sandbox isolation and security end to end, working with Security Engineering on defense in depth for compute, networking, storage, and sensitive information. - Build stateful systems that manage long-lived execution environments and keep user data durable and correct through failures. - Drive performance and efficiency across the stack, from startup latency and resource density to cost. - Run sandbox infrastructure as an always-on production service, setting the bar for reliability, observability, capacity planning, and incident response. - Define clear platform interfaces and APIs so internal teams and external developers can build on sandboxes with confidence. - Provide technical leadership: mentor engineers, write clear design docs, and make long-term architectural decisions that keep the platform simple, secure, and able to evolve. QUALIFICATIONS - Experience designing and running production backend or infrastructure systems - Strong distributed systems experience: you've built and operated systems that coordinate state across many nodes, and you're fluent in consistency, consensus or leader election, idempotency, retries, and failure handling at scale. - Strong system design skills for stateful systems where correctness under failure matters. - Hands-on experience with Linux systems and modern infrastructure (for example AWS, Kubernetes, and container or VM runtimes). - Comfortable with security-sensitive systems and making pragmatic trade-offs between isolation, performance, and velocity. - Collaborative mindset and eagerness to work on hard problems with other experienced engineers. NICE TO HAVE - Experience with Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, KVM, gVisor, Kata, or other virtualization and sandboxing technology. - Experience with snapshotting, copy-on-write filesystems, or block storage. - Experience with Linux networking (namespaces, eBPF, egress filtering) or secrets and key management. - Experience with custom scheduling, multi-cluster orchestration, or distributed state machines. - Experience building developer-facing APIs and SDKs, or code execution and agent infrastructure. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed above.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Solution Consultant - Site Solutions — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Veeva Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Solution Consultant - Site Solutions opportunity with Veeva at Veeva.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: Scale's Generative AI business unit is currently seeing historic levels of growth. As a Strategic Projects Lead (SPL) for Cybersecurity, you will lead cybersecurity data initiatives — building datasets that AI labs buy to train and evaluate their security agents. This role requires deep, hands-on security expertise: you will personally design and quality-audit the vulnerability data, not just coordinate it. You should be prepared to wear many hats (Operator, Product Manager, and customer-facing Engagement Manager), with the technical hat being primary. The ideal candidate has a strong entrepreneurial mindset, is comfortable getting into the weeds, and is excited about intense, impactful work that leads to an accelerated career progression. You will: Design realistic, exploitable vulnerabilities across web application stacks and set the difficulty bar for autonomous security agents. Design and create a QZ process for exploit validity, isolation, and reward-hacking resistance — ensuring a flaw is genuinely hard and the intended path is the only one that reaches success. Lead cross-functional projects with diverse stakeholders (Engineering + Ops + Go-to-Market). Partner with product and engineering teams to enhance our data products for strategic customers and initiatives. Own the execution of our data operations for strategic projects. Give regular progress updates to Scale's executive team. Work on some of the most impactful problems at the company. Ideally, you'd have: Deep, hands-on cybersecurity experience across offensive and defensive work — from exploiting real vulnerabilities (SQLi, SSRF, IDOR, auth bypass, RCE) to understanding how they're detected and remediated. Strong judgment for what makes a security scenario realistic, rigorous, and genuinely challenging — not contrived or trivially solvable. Strong hands-on coding ability — can build, break, and verify web applications (Docker, HTTP, web frameworks); Python data analytics is a baseline, not the core requirement. 3+ years in offensive security/penetration testing, or as a cybersecurity SME; experience leading a team or developing operational processes is a plus. We work closely with leadership and employees to ensure that Datadog continues to scale rapidly, yet smoothly and remains a fantastic place to work. We’re seeking an experienced team member to join our growing global team and play a critical role in keeping Datadogs and our assets safe and secure. You will work directly with the Global Safety & Security Sr Manager - AMER and cross-functional teams to support safety and security operations across the enterprise. Ideal candidates will be passionate about security operations, program development, leadership, project management, customer service and collaboration. This position is based in our New York City headquarters and may require occasional domestic and international travel. The role will focus particularly on three core pillars: Headquarters Security, Global Security Operations Center operations and occasional management of the executive protection program At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. This position requires being in-office 5 days a week. What You’ll Do: Headquarters Security: Manage daily safety and security operations at Datadog’s New York City headquarters, including contract security personnel, access control, visitor management, internal events and incident response. Oversee contract security personnel and vendors, including staffing, training, post orders, service levels, performance reviews and corrective actions. while maintaining a safe, professional and welcoming employee experience. Coordinate with building management, property security and internal teams to coordinate lobby operations, emergency response, life-safety matters and headquarters security incidents.. Identify and address risks associated with operating in a high-profile urban environment, including protests, demonstrations, workplace violence, suspicious activity, property crime and other incidents that may affect Datadogs, visitors or business operations. Develop Security risk mitigation strategies. Support the implementation and management of access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management and other technical security systems. Global Security Operations Center: Advance Datadog’s GSOC as its central hub for global security monitoring, incident intake, triage, escalation, communication and response coordination. Develop and maintain GSOC standard operating procedures, escalation protocols, incident classifications, notification requirements, service levels and quality standards to ensure consistent global operations. Oversee resources supporting GSOC operations, including staffing, training, performance management, vendor relationships and operational readiness. Monitor global events, emerging threats and incidents that could affect Datadog’s employees, offices, executives, travelers, events or operations. Ensure timely and accurate communication during critical incidents, including security alerts, situation reports, leadership briefings and updates to impacted teams. Review incident trends, performance metrics and recurring risks to identify opportunities to improve processes, tools and response capabilities. Lead post-incident reviews and track corrective actions through completion. Executive Protection: Manage and advance Datadog’s executive protection program, including protective intelligence, executive threat monitoring, travel and event security and response to identified or emerging threats. Partner with executives, executive assistants and internal stakeholders to provide security support that is discreet, practical and aligned with Datadog’s culture and business needs when necessary. Manage vendors, ensuring that providers meet Datadog’s expectations for professionalism, confidentiality, service and operational performance. Who You Are: Experienced in managing corporate safety and security operations, ideally within a fast-paced technology environment, with a focus on headquarters security, GSOC operations and executive protection. Skilled in managing all aspects of a physical security program, including contract security personnel, access control, video surveillance, visitor management, event security, investigations and emergency response. Experienced in developing or managing a GSOC, security operations center, command center or similar 24/7 monitoring and incident response capability. Knowledgeable about GSOC operating standards, including incident intake, triage, escalation, communications, reporting, service levels, performance metrics and after-action reviews. Experienced in executive protection program management, including protective intelligence, threat monitoring, executive travel, advance planning, event security and third-party provider management. Able to assess complex or incomplete information, make sound decisions under pressure and communicate clear recommendations during sensitive or rapidly evolving situations. Experienced in conducting physical security and threat assessments, identifying vulnerabilities and developing proportionate mitigation strategies. Knowledgeable about workplace violence prevention, behavioral threat assessment, insider threat, crisis management and active assailant preparedness. Experienced with open-source intelligence, protective intelligence and threat-monitoring tools used to identify and evaluate potential risks involving employees, executives, facilities and business operations. Knowledgeable about technical security systems, with experience supporting physical security design and reviewing access control, surveillance, visitor management and intrusion detection solutions. An exceptional written and verbal communicator who can effectively convey security information across all levels of the organization, with a specific focus on executives and senior leadership. A strong cross-functional partner who can build trusted relationships with internal teams, building management, law enforcement, emergency services, peer organizations and external security providers. Experienced in building and growing safety and security programs that can scale with organizational needs while maintaining a strong employee and customer service focus. Able to exercise a high level of integrity, discretion and confidentiality when managing sensitive incidents, investigations and executive-related matters. Comfortable managing multiple priorities and operating with autonomy in a dynamic environment where risks, business needs and operational requirements may change quickly. 8+ years of progressively responsible experience in corporate security, physical security, GSOC operations, executive protection, law enforcement, intelligence, military security or a related field. 3+ years of experience managing contract security personnel or external security teams Able and willing to travel domestically and internationally and participate in an after-hours on-call rotation. Professional certifications or specialized training in corporate security, executive protection, threat assessment, emergency management or business continuity are preferred. The primary focus of this position is supporting end-to-end delivery of tax features, new-vertical / new-merchant or partnership / new-product launches, and legislative changes on the DoorDash platform, grounded in US sales and use tax, Canada GST/HST/PST, and Australia and New Zealand GST, across food and beverage and retail tax context, with an understanding of how data flows from upstream systems through the tax engine to downstream reporting. Rather than handing off requirements to the Vertex Center of Excellence team, you will apply your own Vertex knowledge to help shape the functional design and recommend the specific Vertex configuration a solution requires. This position may work remotely within the US, but will be based on the East Coast to accommodate EMEA time zones and meetings with global stakeholders. jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As an Applied AI Architect on the Technology Partnerships team at Anthropic, you will be the technical lead for strategic ISV and technology partners building unique product integrations with Claude. These are software companies whose platforms are systems of record for their customers, and who want those customers to be able to work with their data and workflows directly inside Claude. This role goes deep with each partner. You will own the technical side of product partnerships from first scoping through launch and beyond. You will help partners design how their platform shows up in Claude (MCP servers, connectors, plugins, and skills), hold the quality bar through evaluations, and act as the bridge between the partner's product and engineering teams and Anthropic's Product, Engineering, and Research teams. You will be a trusted technical advisor to partner engineering leaders and executives, and you will turn what you learn into patterns and playbooks that make every future integration faster and better. Responsibilities Technical ownership of strategic integrations: Serve as the technical lead for strategic ISV and technology partners building product integrations with Claude. Own the technical plan from use-case definition and scoping through build, launch, and post-launch iteration. Integration architecture: Advise partners on how to expose their platform to Claude, including MCP server design, tool and API surface design for large platforms, authentication and admin onboarding, permissions, and plugin and skill structure. Be opinionated about the patterns that lead to the best experience for joint customers. Evaluations and quality: Design and run evaluations of partner integrations against the use cases that matter most to joint customers. Turn results into concrete, prioritized feedback for partner engineering teams and hold a high quality bar before launch. Hands-on prototyping: Build prototypes, demos, and reference skills that show partners the art of the possible, accelerate their build, and contribute to product improvements. Launch readiness: Partner with Product, Partnerships, Marketing, and GTM teams to get integrations launch-ready on partner-driven timelines such as customer conferences and product events, and support partners and early customers through launch. Product and research feedback loop: Act as the connective tissue between partners and Anthropic's Product, Engineering, and Research teams. Surface integration gaps and platform requirements, help shape the roadmap for how Claude works with third-party software, and bring early capabilities to partners. Executive technical relationships: Build trusted relationships with partner CTOs, product leaders, and engineering leads. Explain technical tradeoffs and Anthropic's point of view clearly to technical and executive audiences alike. Scale what works: Codify reference architectures, integration best practices, evaluation approaches, self-serve guidance, and playbooks so each new technology partnership starts from a stronger foundation, and help enable account teams and the broader partner ecosystem. Joint customer success: Support account teams on strategic joint customers adopting partner integrations, and serve as an escalation point for complex technical issues. You may be a good fit if you have 8+ years of experience in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner Engineer, Developer Relations Engineer, or Technical Account Manager, or as a software engineer on platform, API, or integrations work A track record of leading complex technical integrations with ISVs or technology partners, from solution design through launch Deep experience with APIs, platform integration, and enterprise SaaS architecture, including authentication and authorization models, permissions, and admin experience Hands-on familiarity with LLM applications and agentic tooling, such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), tool use, agents, and evaluation frameworks Strong coding ability; you can build prototypes, write evals, and work in a real codebase (comfort with Python or TypeScript expected) Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders, including C-suite executives and engineering leaders Product sense, and the judgment to know when to push a partner toward a better design and when to adapt to their constraints Comfort operating in early-stage, ambiguous environments where the playbook doesn't exist yet, and a track record of building structure as you go Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. jobs.title: Engineering Manager
jobs.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. About the department Cloudflare's Engineering team builds and runs the software that handles a large share of the Internet's requests. We also build the internal tools and platforms that software depends on. Teams own large areas with real impact and work autonomously within them, whether their customers are external or other Cloudflare engineers. About the team Developer Productivity builds the internal tools and platforms Cloudflare engineers use to take code from commit to production. We own developer infrastructure (CI/CD, build systems), developer insights and ADLC metrics, AI-assisted development, and Cloudflare-on-Cloudflare dogfooding. We're responsible for AI-assisted development across all of Cloudflare engineering, and adoption has grown 4 to 6 times over in the last year. We also own the tooling behind Cloudflare's Engineering Codex, the standards every engineering team is expected to meet. About the role This is a front-line engineering manager role leading a team of 6+ engineers in Bengaluru. The team's initial focus will be on two areas: AI tools for engineers. Agents, agentic systems, MCP servers, evals, and context engineering that change how Cloudflare engineers write, review, and ship code. Engineering standards and the tooling that enforces them. Continuing to transform our Engineering standards into automated guardrails, paved paths, and feedback engineers can act on, instead of checklists and manual review. You'll own the product direction for both areas. There are no dedicated product managers on the team. Our users are Cloudflare engineers, and our engineers work as product engineers who talk to users, watch how tools get used, and help decide what to build next. You'll lead that work, deciding what to build and why, and making sure it gets adopted and solves real problems. You don't need to write code every day, but you should be able to review a design, debug a broken pipeline, or prototype an agent when the team needs it. We move fast. AI tooling changes month to month, so a six-month plan is stale in six weeks. We ship small, put it in front of engineers early, and change course based on what we hear. We'd rather ship a rough version this week and improve it next week than spend a month polishing a design doc. We add process only when it solves a real problem. You'll partner closely with engineering managers and principal engineers in the US, UK, and Europe, and work with teams across Cloudflare's global organization. The team starts in Bengaluru. As it grows, it may include engineers in other regions. What you'll do Hire, onboard, and grow your team. Coach engineers to think like product engineers, run career conversations, give direct feedback, and handle performance. Own the product roadmap. Spend time with the engineers who use your tools, decide which problems matter most, and say no to the rest. Keep the team shipping. Release in small increments, get feedback from users quickly, and cut process that slows the team down without adding value. Deliver in both focus areas: agents, MCP servers, and evals the rest of engineering relies on, and Codex standards turned into CI/CD checks, templates, and policy-as-code, with remediation and exception workflows to match. Measure whether the work is landing: tool adoption, Codex compliance, and what engineers actually think of the experience. Own operations for the platforms your team runs, including on-call and incident response. What we're looking for 3+ years managing software engineers, including hiring, onboarding, and developing people. 8+ years of total software engineering experience, with enough recent hands-on work to hold your own in code and design reviews. Hands-on experience with AI in engineering organizations, such as building agents, running agentic systems in production, or governing how a company uses AI. This is not a model-training or ML research role. Experience building or running developer tools, internal platforms, or CI/CD systems. Product and user thinking. You've owned a roadmap, with or without a PM, and you can point to decisions you made because of what users told you or how they actually used what you built. A bias to action. You've led teams that shipped often and changed direction when the evidence called for it, while still delivering on commitments. Clear judgment and clear writing. You make sound trade-offs and explain the "why" as well as the "how". Much of your work with partners will happen asynchronously across time zones. Bonus points You've built MCP servers or LLM evals, or worked on context engineering for agents. Experience with policy-as-code or compliance automation. Experience measuring developer productivity, using frameworks such as DORA or SPACE, or developer surveys. You've built a team from scratch or started an engineering presence in a new location. Familiarity with TypeScript, Go, or Kubernetes-based systems. What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you! Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs. jobs.title: Recruiting coordinator
jobs.description: ABOUT WATERSHED Watershed https://watershed.com/ is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team. We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us! THE ROLE We are looking for a Recruiting Coordinator to join our team in Mexico City and support our Global talent organization. Our team is responsible for bringing the very best talent to Watershed in order to power the teams working to accelerate the climate economy. It's a rare opportunity to channel your skills into solving one of the most challenging and impactful problems of our generation. We value individuals who are excited to own the coordination process while always striving for excellence and a world class candidate experience. This position is a 6 month contract with the goal of converting to full time. It is based in our Mexico City office 4 days per week. YOU WILL: - Schedule complex phone, virtual, and in-person interviews working across multiple time zones with multiple recruiting partners - Manage logistics for the recruiting process, including room bookings, travel arrangements, and greeting candidates onsite in the Mexico City office - Build strong relationships with our recruiting team and hiring managers to drive an exceptional recruiting process - Own the end-to-end candidate experience while always having an input on improving the recruiting process - Proactively address inefficiencies, leverage our tools/technologies, and implement process improvements - Master our applicant tracking system, scheduling tools, and organizational products, including Ashby, Notion, Google Workspace and Dust YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU: - Have previous experience in a Recruiting Coordinator or other relevant project management or customer service role - Have strong attention to detail with proven operational and systems thinking - Have proven ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a high-demand environment while demonstrating professionalism - Are excited to use AI to drive efficiencies - Are curious and comfortable with ambiguity - Are an excellent verbal and written communicator in English and Spanish - Are passionate about solving climate change and excited to contribute to doing so at a fast-paced startup Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles) Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so. What’s the interview process like? It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process. What if I need accommodations for my interview? At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager, Hardware (Japan)
jobs.description: About the Team The Hardware Marketing team helps people understand what OpenAI’s products can do and how they can fit into everyday life. We work with Product, Design, Creative, Sales, and Operations to bring new products to market and create experiences that let people try them for themselves. About the Role We’re looking for a Product Marketing Manager to lead hardware product marketing in Japan. You’ll define who we should reach in Japan, how we explain the product’s value, and how we bring it to market. You’ll bring Japanese consumer insight into product and launch planning early, so it shapes decisions before the work reaches translation. You’ll report to the International Marketing Lead and also serve as the Asia-Pacific (APAC) marketing lead for Hardware. In that regional role, you’ll coordinate planning with country teams, identify needs they share, and bring market-specific decisions to the global team. In this role, you will: - Get to know customers in Japan. Use research, competitive context, and customer feedback to identify priority audiences, needs, and barriers to adoption. Bring that evidence into product and marketing decisions. - Own positioning and messaging for Japan. Turn global positioning into clear Japanese messaging, locally relevant use cases, and briefs. Work with Product to keep claims accurate and set clear expectations about what the product can do. - Lead go-to-market planning for Japan. Work with Creative, Communications, integrated marketing, and partner-facing teams to carry the product story across campaigns, web, social, retail, and product education. - Get the market ready for launch. Coordinate local materials and dependencies with Product, Operations, and commercial teams. Flag gaps early, agree on owners, and make sure teams have what they need to explain the product to customers. - Coordinate hardware marketing across APAC. Work with country teams on shared planning, surface readiness risks, and identify where markets can reuse work and where they need a different approach. - Use what you learn after launch. Set measures for customer understanding and adoption with Analytics. Use results and feedback to improve messaging, education, and future launch plans. You might thrive in this role if you have: - Led product marketing or go-to-market work for consumer products in Japan, from customer research and positioning through launch. - Made technical products easy to understand without overstating what they can do. Experience with hardware or connected devices is a plus. - Written clear customer-facing messaging in Japanese and worked effectively with global teams in English. - Led work across Product, Creative, Communications, and commercial teams, and can make a clear case for when a global plan should change to meet local needs. - Worked across markets or time zones and used customer feedback and performance data to improve a launch or marketing plan. jobs.title: Finance Fellow - Human Frontier Collective
jobs.description: PLEASE NOTE: This is a fully remote, 1099 independent contractor opportunity with an estimated duration of six months and the potential for extension. This role is open to candidates residing in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada.To be eligible, candidates must be authorized to work in the country they reside in. About the Program The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) Fellowship brings together top researchers and domain experts to collaborate on high-impact work that are shaping the future of AI. As an HFC Fellow, you’ll apply your academic and professional expertise to help design, evaluate, and interpret advanced generative AI systems—while gaining exposure to cutting-edge research and working alongside an interdisciplinary network of leading thinkers. What You'll Do Collaborative Work: Get invited to engage in high-impact projects with our partnered AI labs and platforms. Develop and evaluate complex financial scenarios to test and enhance AI accuracy in valuation, forecasting, and analysis; collaborate in interactive sessions to assess model outputs for market relevance and compliance; provide detailed feedback to improve AI capabilities; and contribute to specialized projects in financial modeling, risk assessment, and equity research. HFC Community: Beyond the work, you’ll become part of a supportive, interdisciplinary network of innovators and thought leaders committed to advancing frontier AI across domains. Contribute to Research Publications: Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers—boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition (e.g., SciPredict , PropensityBench , Professional Reasoning Benchmark ). Who Should Apply Education: PhD, Master, BBA in Finance, Economics, or related degrees. Certifications: CFA or CPA strongly preferred. Professional Background: 5+ years in FP&A, Investment Banking, Portfolio Management, Financial Consulting, or equivalent research experience. Skills: Strong proficiency in financial modeling, valuation methodologies, forecasting, asset pricing, DCF analysis, market analysis, and risk assessment. Professional Mindset: Detail-oriented, innovative thinker with a passion for financial technology and a commitment to collaboration. Prior experience with AI is not required, but a plus. Why Join the HFC? Advance Finance AI Solutions: Apply your financial expertise to solve complex, real-world challenges where your judgment shapes advanced AI reasoning and decision-making. Professional Development: High-impact finance experts expand their influence through review projects, advisory roles, and research—while deepening their AI expertise, sharpening analytical and financial skills, and gaining hands-on experience with cutting-edge AI applications. Join a Top-Tier Network: Collaborate with a global network of academics and experts to advance responsible AI through impactful, flexible research and training. 80% of our members come from leading institutions. Flexible Schedule: Set your own schedule, with flexible 10–40 hour weeks that fit around your life and other commitments. Competitive Pay: Project pay rates vary across platforms and are depending on a number of factors, including but not limited to; projects, scope, skillset, and location. Application Process Apply: We review applications on a rolling basis. Complete a Challenge: Selected candidates will undertake a brief task designed to reflect HFC work and evaluate their domain expertise. Interview: Candidates will get to discuss their research experience, professional background, and alignment with our mission to advance human-centered AI. Join the Collective: Successful candidates will receive an invitation to join the Human Frontier Collective Fellowship. PLEASE NOTE: Our policy requires a 90-day waiting period before reconsidering candidates for the same role. This allows us to ensure a fair and thorough evaluation of all applicants. Our products provide the high-quality data and full-stack technologies that power the world's leading models, and help enterprises and governments build, deploy, and oversee AI applications that deliver real impact. We work closely with industry leaders like Meta, Ernst & Young, Mayo Clinic, Time Inc., the Government of Qatar, and U.S. government agencies including the Army and Air Force. We are expanding our team to accelerate the development of AI applications.
